::: {.entry-meta}
[measurement]{.chip .measured} Entry 35 · milestone M3
:::

M3's third acceptance criterion asks for the end-to-end speed-up of the surrogate inside the
coupling loop, measured and reported. The earlier measurement used the first (v1) surrogate.
The final monotone v3 surrogate had not been timed against TGLF on the same node, because the
scheduler cancelled the prepared job before it started. The [Primer](../primer.qmd) explains
the transport loop; terms are in the [Glossary](../glossary.qmd).

We first looked for the cause of the cancellation in the project's accounting records. The
same record (cancelled by root, zero elapsed time, no reason) appears on seven full-node jobs
since 2 October, and two nodes appear twice; every resubmission ran on another node
([seven full-node jobs since 2 Oct were cancelled by root at start with no reason; each resubmission landed on another node and ran]{.claim}[C-161](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-161){.cid .st-preliminary}). We read this as a node start-up failure rather than a property of the
job. The owner approved a resubmission that excludes those nodes, with one automatic retry.
The retry was not needed.

The job runs the M1 benchmark case (the RAPTOR L-mode scenario) three times on one node with
the same solver, grid and time steps: TGLF itself through TORAX's in-process model, the guarded
v3 surrogate, and QLKNN. Compilation and one warm-up step are timed separately and excluded.
The runner rejects stalled, non-finite and coarse-tolerance solves; none occurred.

| quantity | result |
|---|---|
| run time for 40 steps (TGLF on 51 worker processes, the others on one core) | [TGLF 539.1 s, final v3 surrogate 1.249 s, QLKNN 0.117 s; the v3 surrogate is about 432 times faster than TGLF and 10.7 times slower than QLKNN]{.claim}[C-158](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-158){.cid .st-measured} |
| profile deviation from TGLF at t = 2 s | [final v3 surrogate: T_e 7.7%, T_i 9.2%, n_e 11.4%, psi 0.32%; QLKNN: T_e 155%, T_i 128%, n_e 86%, psi 2.4%]{.claim}[C-159](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-159){.cid .st-measured} |

The v3 surrogate is slower than v1 in the same comparison ([TGLF 540.38 s, v1 surrogate 0.780 s, QLKNN 0.126 s; v1 is about 693 times faster than TGLF]{.claim}[C-132](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-132){.cid .st-measured}). The monotone construction
adds work per evaluation, and the gap to QLKNN remains a recorded ceiling ([K-022](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-022)). Against
TGLF the surrogate stays close in temperature and density, while QLKNN, trained on a different
code, does not reproduce TGLF's profiles in this case.

The surrogate result describes the guarded model, not the network alone. In the final state
the guard sends some faces near the axis and at the edge to the Bohm/gyro-Bohm fallback,
because their inputs lie outside the training box ([17 of 51 faces (rho_tor_norm up to 0.08 and from 0.78) are outside the guard's domain and use the fallback]{.claim}[C-160](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-160){.cid .st-measured}). The comparison is one
trajectory of one case, and the timings come from a single run.

The check is independent of the surrogate's training: TGLF runs inside the loop with its own
transport, and the deviation is measured on the closed-loop profiles, not on single flux
evaluations. Runner, script, source commit and source diff are saved with the outputs.

With this result, all three M3 criteria have evidence for the transport surrogate. M3 stays
open for the RF deposition and pedestal surrogates.
